key_insight: Dynamic surface tension and surfactant adsorption kinetics strongly affect post-impact wetting on rough surfaces, with Surfynol 465 producing the largest covered area, especially at higher surfactant concentration.
engineering_relevance: For spray coating, inkjet printing, and surface treatment on rough substrates, choosing a surfactant with favorable kinetics can materially improve coverage and final wetting uniformity.
method: Experimental drop-impact tests on rough surfaces
Compare three surfactants: Triton X-100, SDS, and Surfynol 465
Vary concentration below and above cmc and analyze coverage area vs. Weber number
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coverage evolution is nearly identical below cmc, while at 2×cmc and higher Weber numbers the surfactants diverge, with Surfynol 465 consistently giving larger final coverage areas.
watch_item: Results are specific to the tested surfactants, concentration range, and surface roughness, so extrapolation to other liquids or textures should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Effect of surfactant kinetics on the wetting following the drop impact onto rough surfaces
